title: Palisade Capital - Supplier Assurance Form Review
summary: Redwood team walked Palisade through the supplier assurance questionnaire (mix of CAIQ and customer specific form). Main asks: SOC 2 scope and recent report, technical details for SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit log retention and log delivery options, data residency for EU customers, and KMS/encryption key management. Agreement to provide SOC 2 cert + scoped evidence, share SSO integration guide, and propose a pilot for log export. Next steps: Redwood to send package and schedule technical follow-up with infra team.
action_items: Owner: Maya Patel; Item: Share SOC 2 report + scoping spreadsheet and CAIQ prefilled answers; Due: 2026-03-09
Owner: Ethan Cho; Item: Create and share SSO (SAML) integration runbook and sample metadata; Due: 2026-03-12
Owner: Sofia Nguyen; Item: Draft proposed audit-log export options (S3 push / syslog / API) with retention costs; Due: 2026-03-11
Owner: Ruth Delgado (customer); Item: Confirm required log retention window and data residency constraints for EU funds; Due: 2026-03-13
next_steps: Redwood to upload SOC 2 report and CAIQ draft to shared folder (link in transcript)
Schedule 1-hour technical deep dive with Palisade infra (Ethan + customer infra) week of Mar 15
Procurement to receive high-level pricing for Dedicated + Private pack options (Maya to follow up)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Sofia Nguyen (Redwood CSM), Dr. Amir Khan (CISO, Palisade), Ruth Delgado (Head of IT Risk), Ben Morris (Procurement), Tara Lee (Legal)
Shared: SOC2 report (link: https://redwood.example.com/soc2/palisade-trial), CAIQ spreadsheet (link: https://drive.example.com/CAIQ-palisade), SSO metadata sample (attachment)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, quick intro — Maya from Redwood, Ethan our SE, Sofia on CSM, and over to you Amir and Ruth for quick intros, please
[00:27] Amir: Hi all, Amir here, CISO at Palisade, I'm primarily interested in scope — what systems handle customer data and where it lives, and how you manage keys etc, we have funds in EU so residency matters
[00:52] Ruth: Hi I'm Ruth, leading IT risk — we'll be walking the supplier assurance form, it's a mix of CAIQ plus our own rows, mainly evidence requests and control owners, hope that's ok
[01:15] Maya: Absolutely, that's the plan. We'll go row by row and flag what we can provide today, what needs an attestation, and where we can provide artifacts. Quick note: transcription may have small mis-words, apologies in advance
[01:35] Ethan: I'll be the technical voice for details like SSO, RBAC, audit logs, encryption and KMS. Happy to jump in when you call those out
[01:50] Ben: Procurement just wants to understand minimum security gating and typical timelines to get evidence — and also whether there's any vendor we we need to involve for dedicated deployments
[02:10] Maya: Great. Opening the CAIQ sheet — first block is organizational security and SOC 2. We maintain SOC 2 Type II for security and availability, scope includes the hosted API and control plane but not customer-managed on-prem installations
[02:36] Amir: Quick Q: is Private (VPC) within that SOC scope if we do a Redwood Private deployment?
[02:50] Ethan: Short answer: the managed control plane and Redwood-managed nodes are in scope; customer-managed on-prem is not. For Private VPC we have two modes — a Redwood-managed control plane on customer VPC (we still control some ops) vs fully air-gapped on-prem where you manage infra — the SOC boundary changes accordingly, we'll call that out in the evidence pack
[03:25] Ruth: Ok please annotate that in the CAIQ answers — there's a specific question on 'service scope and out-of-scope components'
[03:40] Maya: Noted. Next — encryption and key management. We encrypt data at rest and in transit. For hosted we manage keys in KMS, we also support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or customer HSMs for Private. Ethan, can you add brief note about envelope encryption?
[04:05] Ethan: Yeah. We use envelope encryption with CMKs for model artifacts and token cache, and application data is encrypted with per-customer keys when CMK provided. For KMS integration we offer rotation policies and audit events on key usage — these appear in the audit logs. Note: sometimes logs call it K-V cache and it mis-reads as K-V cash in the doc, happy to clarify
[04:38] Amir: Do you provide key usage logs to customers or just internal audits? We need customer visibility into key usage for compliance
[04:52] Ethan: We export key usage events to customer-owned logging endpoints for Private deployments; for hosted we can provide redacted key-usage telemetry and attestations. We'll document exact fields we can share in the pack
[05:15] Tara: Any specifics on encryption algorithms and FIPS compliance?
[05:30] Ethan: AES-256 for data at rest, TLS 1.2+ for transit, and we can support FIPS endpoints in Private environments — we'll list that and the FIPS module versions in the evidence bundle
[05:55] Ruth: Next big section is identity: SSO and RBAC. We run SAML SSO (Okta) and need to map your role model to ours. How granular is Redwood RBAC?
[06:12] Ethan: Our RBAC is tiered: org-admin, app-admin, developer, observer. You can map IdP groups to roles, and we support SCIM provisioning for user sync. For API/Service accounts we have token-based service principal with scoped permissions and expiration policies. We'll include a sample SAML metadata and SCIM mapping file
[06:45] Ben: Is there RBAC audit logging for role changes and admin actions? We need change history for at least two years
[07:00] Ethan: Yes — admin actions, role changes, and token creations are logged. Retention defaults to 90 days on hosted, but for Dedicated/Private we can increase retention and offer S3 export or push to your SIEM. We'll put cost estimates in Sofia's export doc
[07:30] Ruth: The form asks for 'immutable audit log guarantees' — like tamper-evidence. How are logs protected?
[07:45] Ethan: We sign log batches and store them in immutable storage (WORM) in Private deployments; for hosted we provide signed aggregates and attestations from our logging provider. We'll detail options and show sample signed log headers
[08:05] Amir: Data residency — we need EU-only processing for certain funds. Can Redwood guarantee model inference and cache never cross regions?
[08:25] Ethan: We have region pinning and routing policies. For EU-residency we can route inference to EU-hosted pools and keep KV cache in-region. For cross-region fallback we can disable automatic fallback for your account. We'll document regional SLAs and how routing policy works
[08:55] Maya: Note: we'll flag a few open items on network egress for analytics/telemetry that might cross regions for global observability; we'll provide config to opt-out
[09:15] Ruth: Evidence items — the checklist asks for a recent SOC 2 report, encryption config docs, SAML metadata, sample audit logs, and a description of patching windows. Can you provide all those?
[09:33] Maya: Yes. We can provide SOC 2 (redacted), encryption architecture doc, SAML metadata + SCIM mapping, 7 days of sample audit logs with redactions, and our patching cadence document. For longer log retention we'll propose an export job
[09:55] Ben: For procurement we also want SLA language and typical lead times for Dedicated capacity — ballpark numbers now?
[10:10] Maya: Dedicated capacity typical lead time 4–8 weeks depending on GPU type and region; Private/on-prem can be 8–14 weeks. We'll include that in the commercial summary. Pricing tiers we'll follow up separately
[10:30] Amir: On the CAIQ there's a question about penetration testing frequency and bug bounty — what's Redwood's program?
[10:40] Ethan: We do annual pen tests and a continuous internal red team. We run a private bug bounty via a partner and triage critical findings within 72 hours. We'll include the most recent pentest summary with remediation dates in the pack
[11:05] Ruth: A specific ask — do you have an answered UI/API matrix that maps controls to artifacts for easy compliance handoff?
[11:20] Sofia: Yes, we maintain a controls-to-artifacts matrix; I'll attach the latest version that aligns SOC 2 controls to CAIQ and our artifacts (playbook, logs, config exports)
[11:40] Maya: Quick live demo pointer — Ethan can show how to configure SSO mapping and enable log export in the console if we need a technical follow-up
[11:55] Ethan: Quick note: for SAML metadata exchange we typically share an XML file with entityID and assertion consumer service URL; customers supply IdP metadata. We'll add a sample and a checklist for attributes (email, name, groups)
[12:20] Ruth: For legal: are you able to sign our data processing addendum with EU data subprocessors spelled out?
[12:35] Maya: We can sign Palisade's DPA with our standard subprocessors list and will mark region-specific processors, we can run a narrow redline if needed
[12:50] Tara: We'll likely ask for a DPA redline after we get the SOC 2 + CAIQ answers, that's standard
[13:05] Maya: Ok. A few nuance items: cache TTLs for KV cache — we can configure per-customer TTLs and pin cache to region, but model weights are global artifacts — inference is region routed though
[13:25] Ethan: Also worth flagging: for Private air-gapped installs customers manage their own KMS and we have an ops-runbook that describes key injection steps — it's in the doc pack
[13:45] Ben: On evidence delivery, do you prefer a secure share link or direct S3 push? We need that in procurement checklist
[14:00] Sofia: We will upload to a secure share (expiring links) and can also arrange an S3 push to customer-owned bucket for Private/Dedicated entitlements. We'll outline both in the next email
[14:20] Ruth: A small red flag in the form: 'third-party subprocessors and data access' — can you list which third parties have access to logs or telemetry?
[14:35] Maya: We'll include subprocessors list — monitoring vendors, storage, and incident response partners. Access is strictly limited via RBAC and logged; more detail in the evidence list
[14:55] Amir: If we wanted an ISO 27001 cert in addition to SOC 2, do you have it or roadmap?
[15:10] Maya: We do not currently have ISO 27001 cert, it's on the roadmap for later in 2026; we'll share the timeline and controls overlap with SOC 2 in the pack
[15:30] Ethan: Small technical aside: when we say "audit logs" you'll see event types like AUTH_LOGIN, TOKEN_CREATE, ROLE_CHANGE, MODEL_DEPLOY. We'll include a sample JSON event file — note that sometimes transcription spells 'role change' as 'roll change' so watch for OCR-type misreads in exported docs
[15:55] Ruth: For the CAIQ there's a field asking for 'evidence owner contact' — please populate with Redwood contacts per artifact
[16:10] Maya: Will do. Final part: any blockers for pilot? We can run a short pilot with EU region pinning, sample dataset, and 7-day log export so you can validate retention and access patterns — does that sound acceptable?
[16:35] Amir: Yes that would help. We'll need an NDA addendum for the pilot data, and a minimal security questionnaire answered before we start
[16:50] Maya: Noted — we'll attach NDA addendum and prefilled CAIQ. Let's round up with a recap and owners
[17:05] Maya: Recap: Redwood to share SOC 2, prefilling CAIQ, SAML + SCIM runbook (Ethan), audit-log export options (Sofia), and pricing/lead times (Maya). Palisade to confirm retention window and DPA redline. Schedule technical deep dive week of Mar 15.
[17:30] Ruth: Sounds good. One minor transcript note — the auto-transcript sometimes merges names, e.g., "Ethan Cho" might appear as "Ethan Joe" in the raw export, so treat names carefully in evidence docs.
[17:50] Ben: Thanks all.
[18:00] Meeting end
